label: Pembrolizumab SC (Keytruda Qlex) — Song 2025 IV+SC model · 2-compartment · time-varying CL
_note: The popPK model behind the SC approval: Ka, F and sex on Ka estimated on D77 + C18 data, with the whole IV part fixed from the label time-dependent model. The fixed IV part is taken from EMA II/0042, whose values match Song Table 1 exactly; the time-dependence equation is from the Li 2017 NONMEM code.

_source.document: Song et al. 2025, Eur J Cancer 230:115711 (doi:10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115711); EMA assessment report Keytruda EMEA/H/C/003820/II/0042 (2018); Li et al. 2017, J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn (doi:10.1007/s10928-017-9528-y), electronic supplementary NONMEM code
_source.table: Song Table 1 (= FDA Table 52): SC parameters and the fixed IV values; EMA II/0042 Table 10 footnote: covariate equations and references; Li 2017 ESM: equation forms; Song Table 2 and the label: exposures
_source.subjects: 469 patients (MK-3475A-D77: 247 SC 790 mg Q6W and 126 IV 400 mg Q6W; C18 arms 1-3: 96), 6116 samples. The fixed IV model: 2993 patients (KN001/002/006/010/024)

limitations: Relative to the validation values, trough concentrations come out 22~28% lower and AUC 9~18% lower (for both SC and IV; peak concentrations are within ±11%). The representative patient used for comparison (male, ECOG ≥1) is not in any CL-lowering category, whereas the actual population includes 30% women (CL ×0.838) and 35% ECOG 0 (×0.93), giving a geometric-mean CL about 8% lower; the distributions of albumin and other covariates are unknown. The label's geometric-mean CL is also 12~16% lower than the reference subject's. The Q3W accumulation ratio (label 2.5) is off by −10.6% and fails.
The covariance between the between-subject variabilities of CL and Vc is not given anywhere for the final model, so it is set to 0 (the earlier model code has a correlation of about 0.4).

The residual errors of 0.192 (SC) and 0.174 (IV) were inferred to be log-scale standard deviations, as in the parent IV model; no document states this explicitly. The engine cannot take separate values per route, so the SC value 0.192 is used.

Between-subject variability on the magnitude of CL decrease over time (IMAX) (ω² 0.0300, additive) is omitted because the engine does not support it. The FDA reviewer noted that fixing IMAX causes late concentrations after the last dose to be underpredicted.
The equation for the sex effect on the absorption rate is not printed, so it was inferred as (1−0.192) from '19% lower in women'.
The distributions of albumin, bilirubin, tumour size and eGFR in the analysis population are not published, so virtual patients hold these four covariates at their reference values.
The EMA table footnote gives Vc as 3.48, but the body of the same table, Song and the FDA table all give 3.53, so 3.53 is used (3.48 is the earlier model's value).
The source's 'steady state' is cycle 3 (Q6W) or cycle 6 (Q3W), which differs slightly from the app's steady state, where the decrease in CL over time is fully complete.

timeVarying.source: EMA assessment report Keytruda EMEA/H/C/003820/II/0042 (2018) Table 10 (p.24) 'Proposed Updated Label Time-Dependent Model' (N=2993) and its footnote equations — IMAX -0.218 (95% CI -0.254 to -0.157), TI50 65.5 d, Hill 2.99 (all fixed in Song Table 1). Form from Li et al. 2017, J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn (doi:10.1007/s10928-017-9528-y), electronic supplementary NONMEM code: 'TDPK = EXP((...IMAX)*(TIME**HILL)/(TI50**HILL+TIME**HILL))', TVCL = TDPK*...; Li abstract: 'approximately Imax or exactly e^Imax - 1'.
desc: CL(t) = CL0 * exp(-0.218 * t^2.99 / (65.5^2.99 + t^2.99)): maximum decrease 19.6%, half reached at about day 66. Not applied to Q.
